title: Geometric sufficient criterion for all weakly etale covers to split
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring such that $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is w-local [def-weil-pbc-w-local], the quotient space $\pi_0(\operatorname{Spec}R)$ of connected components is extremally disconnected (the closure of every open subset is open), and $R_{\mathfrak m}$ is strictly henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $R$. Then for every commutative ring $B$ and every faithfully flat weakly etale ring map $f:R\to B$ [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map] [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra], there is a ring map $r:B\to R$ satisfying $r\circ f=\mathrm{id}_R$.

proof.text: Apply [thm-weil-pbc-weak-etale-refinement] to $R\to B$, obtaining $B\to E$ faithfully flat and ind-etale and $R\to E$ ind-etale. The composite $R\to E$ is faithfully flat: tensoring an $R$-module complex first with $B$ and then with $E$ preserves and reflects exactness at both stages, as required by [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]. It is weakly etale by [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability]. It suffices to split a further $R$-algebra of $E$, since composing its retraction with $B\to E$ gives the desired map.

Let $I=\bigcap_{\mathfrak m\in\operatorname{MaxSpec}R}\mathfrak m$. W-locality says that the maximal-point subset is Zariski closed, so it equals $V(I)$ by the ideal-zero-locus correspondence. Set $T=V(IE)$. If $q\in T$, its contraction contains $I$ and hence is maximal, say $m$. By base-change stability [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability], $E\otimes_R\kappa(m)$ is weakly etale over the field $\kappa(m)$. Its residue field at $q$ is algebraic by [lem-weil-pbc-weak-etale-field]; indeed all its finitely generated subalgebras are finite etale, so its quotient corresponding to $q$ is an algebraic domain over $\kappa(m)$, hence a field. Since $m$ is maximal this quotient is $E/q$. Thus $q$ is maximal in $E$. Form $S=E_{[T]}$ using [def-weil-pbc-retained-localization]. By [lem-weil-pbc-retained-localization], $E\to S$ is ind-Zariski, $\operatorname{Spec}S$ is w-local, and its closed points are the pairs $(q,q)$ with $q\in T$. A pair $(q,p)$ lies in $V(IS)$ exactly when $I\subseteq p\cap R$. Then $IE\subseteq p\subseteq q$ and both $p,q$ are maximal by the argument just given, so $p=q$. Therefore $V(IS)$ is precisely the closed-point subset of $\operatorname{Spec}S$. Composition gives $R\to S$ ind-etale and weakly etale.

Let $n$ be a maximal ideal of $S$. By step 2, its contraction $m$ in $R$ is maximal. The local map $R_m\to S_n$ is weakly etale: localization is ind-Zariski, and base change and composition preserve weak etaleness [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability]. The base $R_m$ is strictly henselian by hypothesis, so [thm-weil-pbc-weak-etale-strict-local] makes this canonical map an isomorphism. For an arbitrary prime $p\subset S$, choose a maximal $n\supseteq p$. Localizing $R_m\cong S_n$ at the corresponding primes identifies $R_{p\cap R}\cong S_p$; fractions send $r/t$ to $g(r)/g(t)$, so the isomorphism is the canonical local map [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Thus $R\to S$ identifies every local ring.

The map $R\to S$ is weakly etale by step 2, hence flat by the two-flatness definition [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. To prove surjectivity on spectra, take any prime $p$ of $R$ and a maximal $m\supseteq p$. Faithful flatness of $R\to E$ and [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum] give a prime $q$ of $E$ above $m$. It is in $T$, so the retained point $(q,q)$ is a maximal point $n$ of $S$ over $m$. The isomorphism $R_m\cong S_n$ of step 3 carries the prime $pR_m$ to a prime of $S_n$, hence to a prime of $S$ contracting to $p$. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-flat-surjective-spectrum-faithfully-flat] makes $R\to S$ faithfully flat. If $R=0$, then $B=E=S=0$ and the same conclusion holds with empty spectra.

Now apply [lem-weil-pbc-wlocal-stalk-isomorphism-retraction] to $R\to S$. W-locality and the closed-point ideals are supplied by step 2, all local-ring isomorphisms by step 3, and faithful flatness by step 4; extremal disconnectedness is the hypothesis on $R$. Obtain $s:S\to R$ with $s\circ(R\to S)=\mathrm{id}_R$. If $h:E\to S$ and $j:B\to E$ are the construction maps, put $r=s\circ h\circ j$. Then $r\circ f=s\circ(h\circ j\circ f)=\mathrm{id}_R$ by associativity.
